newsitem.title: PERU: Peru hostage says rebel spared his life - paper.
newsitem.headline: Peru hostage says rebel spared his life - paper.

text.p: A top Peruvian official freed during the explosive raid on the Japanese ambassador's home said he could not sleep for thinking about a young rebel who spared his life, a local newspaper reported on Thursday.
"I've hardly slept. I went to bed late and was thinking all the time ... I've remembered and remembered the attitude of that youngster," Agriculture Minister Rodolfo Munante told El Comercio.

Moments after elite Peruvian troops burst on Tuesday afternoon into the building to rescue the 72 hostages held by Marxist gunmen for 126 days, one of the teenage rebels came into the room where high-ranking captives were held and pointed his rifle straight at Munante.
"I don't know what happened, I don't know if he doubted, but I saw sadness in his eyes, maybe because of the order to kill us, or maybe because he saw his life slipping away.
"Then, in a matter of seconds, he turned straight around and closed the door," Munante said.

The rebel, who died along with 13 of his Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) comrades, may have had second thoughts due to the close ties that had formed between captors and captives after 18 weeks inside the residence, he said.
"After so many days of talking and talking an emotional bond had been established."
One hostage -- a Supreme Court judge -- and two commandos also died in the assault which brought a spectacular end to Latin America's longest hostage siege.
